title: Anna's Reel
author: Rick Mohr
notes: The Caller's Box 140, permission: full. **A two-pass record** (M8): the phrase list holds both passes in order, `A1 A2 B1 B2 2A1 2A2 2B1 2B2`, and `passes: 2` says so. The set progresses at the end of **each** pass, and the second pass exchanges the roles throughout — which is why it is written out rather than derived, and which is the consequence of the progression below rather than a coincidence. A1's wave of four runs **across** the set (`balance-wave-of-four`). **The swap-sides progression is a record field** (M8b): `"progression": { "places": { "lark": 1, "robin": 1 }, "line": "swap" }` — one dancing place along and everybody crosses to the other line, keeping the way they were travelling, which is the Caller's Box's own "other; single, swap sides" and puts the other role on each line, so the second pass is the first danced by the other role. Measured, it is the right mechanism: **closure went from 20.0000/37.7359 px at every length to 0.0000 at 2, 4 and 6 couples**, and reach from 25.5193 px short to 0.2194. `37.7359` was always `sqrt(32^2 + 20^2)`, across the set *and* one place along, and the 32 is the swap. **Still owed, two things, measured.** (1) `collision 0.000 px` at every length, at **beat 32**: A2's nine-beat half hey leaves two of its four dancers on one floor point (`c1/lark` and `c1/robin` both on (24, 30) at 4 couples), which is M5's "a hey that ends short settles on the two places it stopped between" settling two dancers on one place. (2) closure still fails at the **odd** lengths — 37.7359 px at 3 couples and 32.0000 at 5 — where a duple improper line has a waiting couple and the swap has a second end effect the lattice shift does not reproduce.
